summary: Iteration 64 - Feature 'Precio por persona segun ocupacion' (presentation-only helper). Ran 11 pytest cases (6 unit + 5 e2e) all PASSING; validated exact-to-the-cent sum in multiple scenarios (8pax 2triples+1doble, rounding residual on 7 pax, custom single-row, final_total con descuento, menores). E2E: created a real package quotation with pax.rooms=[{triple:2},{doble:1}], verified GET /api/quotations/{id} returns per_person_breakdown, PATCH persists show_per_person, public GET /api/public/quotations/{token} exposes breakdown, PDF returns 200 application/pdf. Frontend UI verified: /app/quotations/{id} renders data-testid=per-person-breakdown with pp-row-triple/pp-row-doble (Triple 6pax $10,263.16 /persona; Doble 2pax $11,710.53 /persona) and public /q/{token} renders data-testid=public-per-person-breakdown with matching rows and Total final $85,000.02 MXN. Sum 6*10263.16 + 2*11710.53 = 85,000.02 = total exacto al centavo.
critical_code_review_comments: pricing_breakdown.py is well isolated: consumes items+total, never touches pricing.py. Contract 'sum(rows.subtotal) == total exactly' is enforced by residual absorption on the largest row - verified for rounding case (3200/7).
PATCH /api/quotations/{id} filters {k:v for ...items() if v is not None} - explicit False for show_per_person still gets persisted (since False is not None). Good.
public_payments.py builds per_person_breakdown inline every request - fine (helper is cheap). Uses final_total via helper's own final_total>total fallback. Consistent with detail endpoint.
